svg.title: Compare Accepted-Appointment Fee Hypotheses
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-subniche-accepted-appointment-yields; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Compare Accepted-Appointment Fee Hypotheses; subtitle: Five commercial sub-niches use the same unit: operator service revenue per client-accepted appointment.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: USD per accepted appointment, excluding retainers and advertising pass-through. Prices are deliberately illustrative quote hypotheses, not market averages or incremental revenue to add to the scorecard. Only the $1,000 hypothesis feeds the Base funnel. ACH and card describe collection methods; processing expenses belong in costs and do not change the gross-fee comparison.; caption: Validate each fee against client gross contribution, close rate, attendance, and replacement burden. A $1,000 appointment at a 20% close rate implies $5,000 in appointment fees per won client before retainers and the client's own selling costs.; stages: label: Commercial HVAC service; value: $1,000 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 1000.0; detail: Require an in-territory commercial site, relevant equipment scope, and an authorized facilities contact. Reject residential requests and emergency calls outside staffed coverage.; label: Managed IT services; value: $900 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 900.0; detail: Verify employee or endpoint range, incumbent-provider context, and a business decision-maker. Reject consumer device support and accounts below the contracted service minimum.; label: Industrial equipment maintenance; value: $800 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 800.0; detail: Capture equipment category, site location, maintenance need, and purchasing responsibility. Reject unsupported equipment and work outside the client's field-service territory.; label: Contract logistics services; value: $700 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 700.0; detail: Confirm shipment frequency, lane coverage, cargo category, and commercial procurement ownership. Reject one-time consumer moves and lanes the client cannot economically serve.; label: Commercial cleaning contracts; value: $600 accepted appointment fee, collected through card invoicing.; numeric value: 600.0; detail: Verify facility size, recurring service frequency, access requirements, and decision authority. Reject residential cleaning and sites below the client's minimum monthly contract.

rect.title: label: Commercial HVAC service; value: $1,000 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 1000.0; detail: Require an in-territory commercial site, relevant equipment scope, and an authorized facilities contact. Reject residential requests and emergency calls outside staffed coverage.

label: Managed IT services; value: $900 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 900.0; detail: Verify employee or endpoint range, incumbent-provider context, and a business decision-maker. Reject consumer device support and accounts below the contracted service minimum.

label: Industrial equipment maintenance; value: $800 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 800.0; detail: Capture equipment category, site location, maintenance need, and purchasing responsibility. Reject unsupported equipment and work outside the client's field-service territory.

label: Contract logistics services; value: $700 accepted appointment fee, collected through ACH invoicing.; numeric value: 700.0; detail: Confirm shipment frequency, lane coverage, cargo category, and commercial procurement ownership. Reject one-time consumer moves and lanes the client cannot economically serve.

label: Commercial cleaning contracts; value: $600 accepted appointment fee, collected through card invoicing.; numeric value: 600.0; detail: Verify facility size, recurring service frequency, access requirements, and decision authority. Reject residential cleaning and sites below the client's minimum monthly contract.
